{{Short description|Final of the 2025–26 EFL Cup}} {{Use dmy dates|date=January 2026}} {{Infobox football match | title = 2026 EFL Cup final | other_titles = | image = London Wembley.jpg | caption = [[Wembley Stadium]] hosted the final. | event = [[2025–26 EFL Cup]] | team1 = [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] | team1score = 0 | team2 = [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] | team2score = 2 | details = | date = {{Start date|2026|3|22|df=y}} | stadium = [[Wembley Stadium]] | city = [[London]] | man_of_the_match1a = [[Nico O'Reilly]] ([[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]]) | referee = [[Peter Bankes]] ([[Lancashire County Football Association|Lancashire]]){{cite news |title=Referee Appointments: Carabao Cup Final 2026 |url=https://www.efl.com/news/2026/march/11/referee-appointments--carabao-cup-final-2026/ |website=EFL.com |publisher=The English Football League |date=11 March 2026 |accessdate=20 March 2026 }} | attendance = 88,486 | weather = | previous = [[2025 EFL Cup final|2025]] | next = ''[[2027 EFL Cup final|2027]]'' }} The '''2026 EFL Cup final''' was the final match of the [[2025–26 EFL Cup]]. The match took place on 22 March 2026 at [[Wembley Stadium]] in [[London]], England,{{cite web |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/soccer/2026/02/03/when-carabao-cup-final-arsenal/88493088007/ |title=When is Carabao Cup final? Arsenal beats Chelsea, awaits Man City-Newcastle winner |website=[[USA Today]] |date=3 February 2026 |access-date=4 February 2026|first=Jesse |last=Yomtov}} between [[Arsenal F.C.–Manchester City F.C. rivalry|rivals]] [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] and [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]].{{cite web |url=https://www.efl.com/news/2026/february/03/arsenal-reach-carabao-cup-final-after-last-gasp-joy-/ |title=Arsenal reach Carabao Cup Final after last-gasp Havertz goal|website=EFL.com |publisher=English Football League|date=3 February 2026 |access-date=4 February 2026}} The clubs have met in the [[2018 EFL Cup final]] as well as in the [[2014 FA Community Shield]] and the [[2023 FA Community Shield]] —with the latter being [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]]'s most recent competitive title. This was [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]]'s ninth League Cup final, the first EFL Cup final since losing to City in the [[2018 EFL Cup final]], and the first appearance in any final since the [[2020 FA Cup final]]. They were seeking their first major trophy since winning the [[2019–20 FA Cup]] and a first League Cup title since the [[1993 Football League Cup final]]. This was [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]]'s tenth League Cup final and the first EFL Cup final since their most recent win in the [[2021 EFL Cup final]] against [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]] to secure their eighth overall and joint-record fourth consecutive title. They were looking for their first major cup competition title since winning the [[2022–23 UEFA Champions League]].{{efn|Excluding their subsequent triumphs in the [[2023 UEFA Super Cup]], [[2023 FIFA Club World Cup]], and [[2024 FA Community Shield]], which are not considered as "major titles", as well as the [[2023–24 Premier League]], which is not a cup competition.}} ==Route to the final== {{main|2025–26 EFL Cup}} ===Arsenal===

As a Premier League club involved in [[UEFA club competitions|UEFA competitions]], Arsenal entered in the third round and were drawn away to [[EFL League One]] club [[Port Vale F.C.|Port Vale]]. At [[Vale Park]], on 24 September 2025, Arsenal won 2–0 with goals from [[Eberechi Eze]] – his first goal for the club – and [[Leandro Trossard]].{{Cite web |date=24 September 2025 |first=Gary |last=Rose|title=Port Vale 0-2 Arsenal: Eberechi Eze score first Gunners goal in EFL Cup win |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/c5ygpez5znyt |access-date=4 February 2026 |website=BBC Sport}} In the fourth round Arsenal were drawn at home to fellow [[Premier League]] club [[Brighton & Hove Albion F.C.|Brighton & Hove Albion]]. At the [[Emirates Stadium]] on 29 October 2025, Arsenal won 2–0 again with goals for the Gunners from [[Ethan Nwaneri]] and [[Bukayo Saka]] which sent the Gunners through to the quarter-finals.{{Cite web |date=29 October 2025 |title=Arsenal 2-0 Brighton: Ethan Nwaneri and Bukayo Saka goals send Arsenal through |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/cd9k0xe2nlkt |first=Alex |last=Howell |access-date=4 February 2026 |website=BBC Sport}} In the quarter-finals Arsenal were drawn against another Premier League club in [[Crystal Palace F.C.|Crystal Palace]]. At the Emirates Stadium on 23 December 2025, Arsenal drew 1–1 with an [[own goal]] from [[Maxence Lacroix]] being equalised by [[Marc Guéhi]]. As the game finished level after regulation time, it went straight to a [[Penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalty shoot-out]] which Arsenal won 8–7 with [[Martin Ødegaard]], [[Declan Rice]], Saka, Trossard, [[Mikel Merino]], [[Riccardo Calafiori]], [[Jurriën Timber]] and [[William Saliba]] all scoring their spot-kicks for the Gunners and [[Jean-Philippe Mateta]], [[Justin Devenny]], [[Will Hughes]], [[Borna Sosa]], [[Jefferson Lerma]], [[Adam Wharton]] and [[Christantus Uche]] all converted their penalty kicks; Lacroix missed the decisive penalty kick to send Arsenal through to the semi-finals.{{Cite web |date=23 December 2025 |first=Alex |last=Howell |title=Arsenal beat Crystal Palace on penalties for place in EFL Cup semi-final against Chelsea|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/live/c0582m4n108t |access-date=4 February 2026 |website=BBC Sport}} In the semi-finals Arsenal were drawn against another fellow [[Premier League]] club and [[Arsenal F.C.–Chelsea F.C. rivalry|rivals]] [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]] over two legs. Arsenal won the first leg 3–2 at [[Stamford Bridge (stadium)|Stamford Bridge]] on 14 January 2026 with two goals for Chelsea from [[Alejandro Garnacho]] and goals for Arsenal from [[Ben White (footballer)|Ben White]], [[Viktor Gyökeres]] and [[Martín Zubimendi]].{{Cite web |date=14 January 2026 |title=Chelsea 2-3 Arsenal: Viktor Gyokeres ends goal drought as Gunners edge first leg of Carabao Cup semi-final |url=https://www.skysports.com/football/news/11095/13493486/chelsea-2-3-arsenal-viktor-gyokeres-ends-goal-drought-as-gunners-edge-first-leg-of-carabao-cup-semi-final |access-date=4 February 2026 |website=Sky Sports}}{{Cite web |date=14 January 2026 |title=Chelsea 2-3 Arsenal: Gunners have EFL Cup semi-final advantage but Garnacho gives Blues hope|first=Nizaar |last=Kinsella |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/cp82v1qp9e1t |access-date=5 February 2026 |website=BBC Sport}} Arsenal won the second leg 1–0 at the Emirates Stadium on 3 February 2026 with a goal from former Chelsea player [[Kai Havertz]] to give Arsenal a 4–2 aggregate victory and send them through to the final.{{Cite web |date=3 February 2026 |title=Carabao Cup: Arsenal beat Chelsea to reach first major cup final for almost six years|first=Alex |last=Howell |url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/live/c07xyy0j4l5t|access-date=4 February 2026 |website=BBC Sport}} ===Manchester City===
{| class="wikitable plainrowheaders" style="text-align:center;float:right" |- !scope=col style="width:25px"| Round !scope=col style="width:200px"| Opposition !scope=col style="width:90px"| Score |- !scope=row style="text-align:center"| 3 | [[Huddersfield Town A.F.C.|Huddersfield Town]] ([[Kirklees Stadium|A]]) | 2–0 |- !scope=row style="text-align:center"| 4 | [[Swansea City A.F.C.|Swansea City]] ([[Swansea.com Stadium|A]]) | 3–1 |- !scope=row style="text-align:center"| QF | [[Brentford F.C.|Brentford]] ([[City of Manchester Stadium|H]]) | 2–0 |- !rowspan="2" scope=row style="text-align:center"| SF | [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]] ([[St James' Park|A]]) | 2–0 |- | Newcastle United ([[City of Manchester Stadium|H]]) | 3–1 |- |colspan="3"| '''Key:''' (H) = Home; (A) = Away |}
As a Premier League club involved in UEFA competitions, Manchester City entered in the third round and were drawn away to [[EFL League One]] club [[Huddersfield Town A.F.C.|Huddersfield Town]]. At [[Kirklees Stadium]], on 24 September 2025, Manchester City won 2–0 with goals from [[Phil Foden]] and [[Savinho]].{{cite web |title=Foden, Savinho score as Man City ease past Huddersfield |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/report/_/gameId/758198 |agency=[[PA Media]]|website=ESPN|date=24 September 2025 |access-date=4 February 2026}} In the fourth round, they were drawn away to [[EFL Championship]] side [[Swansea City A.F.C.|Swansea City]], played away at [[Swansea.com Stadium]] on 29 October 2025. The match finished 3–1 for the visitors, with [[Gonçalo Franco]] opening the scoring for Swansea City before three goals from [[Jérémy Doku]], [[Omar Marmoush]] and [[Rayan Cherki]] for Manchester City.{{cite web |title=Erling Haaland sits as Man City reach Carabao Cup quarters |agency=PA Media |url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/report/_/gameId/759243 |access-date=4 February 2026|website=ESPN |date=29 October 2025}} In the quarter-finals, City were drawn at home to fellow Premier League side [[Brentford F.C.|Brentford]], where they won 2–0 at [[City of Manchester Stadium]] on 17 December 2025 with goals from Cherki and Savinho.{{cite web |title=Cherki channels Haaland in leading Man City to Carabao Cup semifinals|url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/report/_/gameId/760343 |agency=[[Associated Press]] |website=ESPN|access-date=4 February 2026|date=17 December 2025}} In the two-legged semi-final, City were drawn against [[2025 EFL Cup final|cup holders]] [[Newcastle United F.C.|Newcastle United]], with the first leg played at [[St James' Park]] on 13 January 2026. City won 2–0 courtesy of freshly-signed [[Antoine Semenyo]] and Cherki.{{cite web |title=Semenyo scores again as Man City get semifinal edge over Newcastle|url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/report/_/gameId/401842433 |agency=PA Media |website=ESPN|access-date=4 February 2026 |date=13 January 2026}} The second leg was played on 4 February, with Manchester City winning 3–1. Marmoush scored twice and [[Tijjani Reijnders]] scored once before [[Anthony Elanga]] picked up a consolation goal for Newcastle, giving Manchester City a 5–1 aggregate victory and sending them to the final.{{cite web |title=Manchester City roll past Newcastle into cup final with Arsenal|url=https://www.espn.com/soccer/report/_/gameId/401842434|website=ESPN|agency=PA Media |access-date=4 February 2026 |date=4 February 2026}} {{clear}} ==Match== === Background === This saw Arsenal play in their first major cup final since the [[2020 FA Cup final|2020 final]], which they won against [[Arsenal F.C.–Chelsea F.C. rivalry|London rivals]] [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]], and seek their second major trophy under the management of their former player and captain [[Mikel Arteta]]. This final was a repeat of the [[2018 EFL Cup final|2018 final]], when [[Arsène Wenger]]'s Arsenal lost 3–0 to City, with Arteta as [[Pep Guardiola]]'s assistant manager. Heading into the match, Arsenal could still win the [[List of association football teams to have won four or more trophies in one season|quadruple]] of the EFL Cup, the [[2025–26 FA Cup|FA Cup]], the [[2025–26 Premier League|Premier League]] and the [[2025–26 UEFA Champions League|UEFA Champions League]], which would be the first time an English team has achieved such a feat. The clubs have been [[Arsenal F.C.–Manchester City F.C. rivalry|rivals]] since 2008, and competed for the Premier League title in the [[2022–23 Premier League|2022–23]] and [[2023–24 Premier League|2023–24]] seasons, with City winning on both occasions. === Team selection === [[Mikel Arteta]] made two changes from [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]]'s previous match a 2–0 home win (and a 3–1 aggregate victory) over [[Bundesliga]] club [[Bayer 04 Leverkusen|Bayer Leverkusen]] in the last 16 of the [[2025–26 UEFA Champions League|UEFA Champions League]] with cup goalkeeper [[Kepa Arrizabalaga]] coming in for number 1 [[David Raya]] and [[Kai Havertz]] replacing the injured [[Eberechi Eze]] with [[Jurriën Timber]] and captain [[Martin Ødegaard]] both also missing the final through injury with [[Ben White (footballer)|Ben White]] starting in place of Timber.{{Cite web |date=2026-04-04 |title=Team news: Havertz and Kepa to start at Wembley |url=https://www.arsenal.com/news/team-news-havertz-and-kepa-start-wembley |access-date=2026-03-23 |website=Team news: Havertz and Kepa to start at Wembley |language=en}} Meanwhile, [[Pep Guardiola]] made four changes from [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]]'s previous match a 2–1 home defeat (and a 5–1 aggregate defeat) to [[La Liga]] club [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] in the last 16 of the [[2025–26 UEFA Champions League|UEFA Champions League]], with Guardiola sticking with cup goalkeeper [[James Trafford]] over number 1 [[Gianluigi Donnarumma]] with [[Nathan Aké]] in central defence and [[Nico O'Reilly]] at left-back, they replaced the injured [[Rúben Dias]] and [[Rayan Aït-Nouri]] and [[Antoine Semenyo]] took the place of [[Tijjani Reijnders]] further forward.{{Cite web |last=Mumford |first=Jack |title=Four changes for Carabao Cup final as Trafford starts |url=https://www.mancity.com/news/mens/Four%20changes%20for%20Carabao%20Cup%20final%20as%20Trafford%20starts |access-date=2026-03-23 |website=Manchester City FC |language=en}} === Summary === ==== First half ==== [[Arsenal F.C.|Arsenal]] kicked-off the first-half in front of 88,486 spectators with [[Kai Havertz]] having the first chance of the match for Arsenal which was saved by City goalkeeper [[James Trafford]] after a shot from the right side of City's six yard box after an assist from [[Martín Zubimendi]] and captain [[Bukayo Saka]] then saw his shot for Arsenal saved by [[James Trafford]] in the 7th minute from a tight angle on the right and [[Bukayo Saka]]'s follow-up shot was also saved by [[James Trafford]]. [[Leandro Trossard]] then saw his shot blocked by the City defence in the 12th minute after a shot from outside the box and [[Piero Hincapié]] then received the first yellow card of the match from referee [[Peter Bankes]] in the 16th minute for a foul on [[Matheus Nunes]]. [[Abdukodir Khusanov]] then received the second yellow card of the match in the 32nd minute for a foul on [[Viktor Gyökeres]]. [[Piero Hincapié]] then missed his shot for Arsenal in the 38th minute with a header from the left side of City's six yard box was too high after a [[corner kick]] from captain [[Bukayo Saka]] and [[Jérémy Doku]] then had his left footed shot for City blocked by the Arsenal defence from the left side of Arsenal's box in the 44th minute. In the final action of the opening half [[Erling Haaland]] missed his shot for City in the 45th minute after his header was too high after a [[Cross (association football)|cross]] from [[Antoine Semenyo]].{{Cite web |last=EFL |date=2026-03-22 |title=Carabao Cup Final report: Arsenal 0-2 Man City |url=https://efl.com/news/2026/march/22/carabao-cup-final-report--arsenal-0-2-man-city/ |access-date=2026-03-23 |website=EFL |language=en}} ==== Second half ==== [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]] kicked off the second half with [[Erling Haaland]] having his shot for City blocked from the centre of Arsenal's penalty box after a [[Cross (association football)|cross]] from [[Antoine Semenyo]] in the 49th minute and [[Kai Havertz]] then had his left-footed shot from a tight angle on the left blocked by the City defence in the 50th minute. [[Kepa Arrizabalaga]] then received Arsenal's second yellow card in the 50th minute after coming out of his box and pulling down [[Jérémy Doku]] and [[Rodri (footballer, born 1996)|Rodri]] then had his right-footed shot from outside the box blocked by the Arsenal defence following an assist from [[Rayan Cherki]] in the 55th minute. [[Antoine Semenyo]] then missed his left-footed shot for City from the right side of Arsenal's box in the 57th minute and [[Rayan Cherki]] then had his left-footed shot from the centre of Arsenal's box blocked by their defence in the 58th minute. [[Nathan Aké]] then had his left-footed shot from the centre of Arsenal's box blocked by the Arsenal defence in the 60th minute. [[Nico O'Reilly]] then opened the scoring for City with a header from a [[Cross (association football)|cross]] from the right by [[Rayan Cherki]] in the 60th minute after a mistake by [[Kepa Arrizabalaga]]. [[Nico O'Reilly]] then doubled City's lead with another header from a [[Cross (association football)|cross]] by [[Matheus Nunes]] in the 64th minute from the right. [[Mikel Arteta]] then made a double substitution for Arsenal in the 65th minute with [[Riccardo Calafiori]] replacing [[Piero Hincapié]] and [[Noni Madueke]] replacing [[Kai Havertz]]. [[Ben White (footballer)|Ben White]] was then booked for Arsenal in the 69th minute for a foul on [[Rayan Cherki]]. [[Riccardo Calafiori]] then saw his header from the centre of City's box saved in the top centre of the goal by [[James Trafford]] after [[Cross (association football)|a cross]] from [[Declan Rice]]. [[Riccardo Calafiori]] then hit the right post of City's goal with a left-footed shot from the left side of City's box after a headed pass from [[Leandro Trossard]] in the 78th minute. [[Mikel Arteta]] then made another double substitution for Arsenal in the 82nd minute with [[Gabriel Martinelli]] replacing [[Leandro Trossard]] and [[Gabriel Jesus]] replacing [[Ben White (footballer)|Ben White]]. [[Gabriel Jesus]] then hit the bar of City's goal with a header from a tight angle on the left after a [[Cross (association football)|cross]] from [[Noni Madueke]] and captain [[Bukayo Saka]] then missed his left-footed shot for Arsenal from the centre of City's box after an assist from [[Declan Rice]]. [[Jérémy Doku]] then missed his right-footed shot for City from outside Arsenal's box, which was close after an assist from [[Nathan Aké]]. [[Pep Guardiola]] then made what turned out to be City's sole substitution with [[Phil Foden]] replacing [[Rayan Cherki]] in the 90th minute with the match ending 2–0 to Manchester City to give them their first [[EFL Cup]] triumph since the [[2021 EFL Cup final]] against [[Tottenham Hotspur F.C.|Tottenham Hotspur]] and meant that it denied Arsenal the chance of winning an unprecedented [[List of association football teams to have won four or more trophies in one season|quadruple]] of the [[2025–26 FA Cup|FA Cup]], the [[2025–26 EFL Cup|EFL Cup]], the [[2025–26 UEFA Champions League|UEFA Champions League]] and the [[2025–26 Premier League|Premier League]].{{Cite web |last=EFL |date=2026-03-22 |title=Carabao Cup Final report: Arsenal 0-2 Man City
